thread:
ops-bot: alert — increased preemptible GPU interruptions in us-west1 starting 2026-03-18T02:04Z. 60% of nodes in pool 'gpu-preemptible-mix-a' reported SIGTERM within 7m.

sre-oncall: seeing p95/p99 generation latency spike to ~2.2s and 5s respectively across hosted endpoints (us-west1). Some canaries degraded.

maya: confirmed — eviction logs show cloud-provider preemption wave around 02:02–02:10 UTC. evict_count: 118, affected_pods: 42.

leo: how much of traffic is on the preemptible pool vs dedicated right now?

samina: about 55% of low-priority inference traffic routed to preemptible pool (batching jobs + cheap realtime tiers). Dedicated handles the rest.

cost-ops: rough cost note: preemptible mix reduces spend ~40% normally. If we shift to dedicated for a few hours, cost delta ~+0.6x for the window.

maya: mitigation idea — trigger graceful-drain of the affected AZ, and route new requests to fallback set (on-demand/dedicated in other AZs). Need quick canary for cold-starts.

leo: can we enable fast failover policy? current policy retries once with 300ms backoff. propose: retry 3x with exponential backoff up to 1.5s and immediate fallback to on-demand model variant.

sre-oncall: doing that now — updating routing policy to: retries=3, initial_backoff=250ms, max_backoff=1500ms, fallback_group=dedicated-us-west1-b. Will roll in 30s.

ops-bot: deploy-bot reported: routing-config change started by sre-oncall at 02:12Z.

maya: also caching note — prefix KV cache warmed on preemptible pool but not on dedicated variants. we should prime cache before shifting significant traffic.

leo: agree. plan: 1) spin up 6 smaller on-demand instances in us-west1-b (gpu-small), 2) enable routing change, 3) run cache-warm job for 10 minutes, 4) observe p99 for 15m.

samina: who will own the spin-up? I can take infra steps (terraform apply) if someone gives the green light.

cost-ops: ack — please tag resources with emergency:preemptible-fallback so we can reconcile cost later.

maya: below gcloud snippet for quick spin up (use our internal image id):

```
# one-off quick pool
gcloud compute instances create gpu-small-ep-{1..6} \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-t4,count=1 \
  --image=projects/redwood-images/global/images/redwood-gpu-rt-2026-02-15 \
  --zone=us-west1-b \
  --metadata=pool=dedicated-fallback,owner=samina,emergency=true
```

samina: starting terraform plan -> apply in 2m.

leo: I'll prepare the cache-warm job. warm list = frequently used prompts + top 50 embeddings. run with concurrency=4.

sre-oncall: routing changes live. initial metrics look better: p95 down from 2.2s -> 1.0s within 90s. p99 still at ~2.1s.

cost-ops: note for finance — we expect an incremental ~$1.8k/hour while fallback is active.

maya: re: root cause — cloud provider indicated a capacity reclaim due to internal maintenance in us-west1 primary cluster. They flagged it as a planned reclaim but with mismatched ETA; our preemptible SLAs caught us off guard.

leo: longer-term action: reduce single-AZ concentration in preemptible pool, add proactive draining thresholds (e.g., if evictions > 10 in 5m, shift 30% traffic off preemptible), and introduce ephemeral on-demand buffer instances that can auto-start on preemption noise.

samina: will open infra ticket with implementation plan + terraform modules for ephemeral buffer. linking ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-3089

maya: also recommend updating autoscaler to consider eviction-rate as a signal (not just CPU/GPU utilization).

sre-oncall: agreed. quick follow-up items:
- @samina spin up fallback pool and tag resources (in progress)
- @leo start cache warm job (in progress)
- @cost-ops track spend and notify if exceeds $3k/hr
- @maya file post-incident summary + RCA draft

samina: fallback pool up (6 instances) and registered to dedicated-us-west1-b pool.

leo: cache-warm job started at 02:18Z. 10m warm completed, hit ratio ~87% on warmed prefixes.

ops-bot: prometheus alerts: gpu_preemptible_eviction_rate returned to baseline 02:36Z.

sre-oncall: p99 back to ~750ms at 02:40Z, traffic normalized. marking incident as mitigated.

maya: RCA notes in progress: preemptible reclaim due to provider maintenance + high single-AZ weight + lack of eviction-signal-based routing.

cost-ops: final cost estimate so far ~ $2.1k for the event window. We'll reconcile in monthly report.

leo: follow-up action items for next sprint: implement eviction-based routing thresholds, ephemeral buffer autoscaling, and cross-AZ preemptible diversification.

sre-oncall: great work team. closing thread after RCA published. :thumbsup:
